subject: Late-sprint node tally and deal ops check — HelioFoundry POC
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Susan Kim <susan.kim@heliofoundry.com>
Date: 2028-06-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Late-sprint node tally and deal ops check — HelioFoundry POC

Folks,

HelioFoundry is moving to a late-stage POC and asked for an operational readiness check before they sign the SOW. High-level ask from the customer: a 6-week dedicated sprint starting ~2028-08-15 with an expected steady-state of ~32 GPU slots (they specify A100-class performance; they told us to assume 80GB profiles for parts of the workload).

Can we do a quick inventory and say whether we can: 1) carve a contiguous 32-slot block in us-west for the requested window, 2) offer a fallback plan if us-west has maintenance events, and 3) propose a safety buffer (we normally recommend +10–20%).

I attached the mutual action plan they've been iterating on (MAP_v2.xlsx) — customer expects us to mark capacity as "reserved/soft" while legal finalizes the SOW. Timeline is tight: Helio procurement wants a formal response by Monday EOD so they can align budget approvals.

Quick asks:
- Rishi: rough availability across us-west/us-central for Aug 15–Sep 30 window
- Irene: any maintenance or fleet events planned in that window that would affect capacity
- Jonas: if ops confirms, can we issue a short-lived soft-hold (14 days) to buy time for final SOW?

Thanks — Ben

[attachment: MAP_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Susan Kim <susan.kim@heliofoundry.com>
Date: 2028-06-24T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Late-sprint node tally and deal ops check — HelioFoundry POC

Ben — thanks for the heads-up. I'll coordinate with infra now. High-level plan I propose:

1) Tally and map: Rishi to run a quick inventory query (by rack/pod/thermal bin) and surface contiguous allocation candidates.
2) Soft-hold: If inventory shows >=32 contiguous slots in us-west, we put a 14-day soft-hold flag in the provisioning system tied to DEAL-8421. Soft-hold = prevents new allocations but not hard commit.
3) Fallback: If contiguous block is not available in us-west, propose split allocation (24 us-west + 8 us-central) with routing policy to keep latency-sensitive traffic in us-west.
4) Buffer: propose reserving 36 slots (12.5% buffer) and a plan to spill to burst pool if the buffer is insufficient.

Ben, please confirm if Helio will accept a split allocation as a fallback. Susan, if we proceed with a soft-hold, we'll provide a short note for procurement documenting the hold mechanics and the next steps for converting to a hard commit.

I'll wait for Rishi and Irene's availability numbers and planned maintenance windows and will then action the soft-hold if we have the headroom.

— Jonas

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Susan Kim <susan.kim@heliofoundry.com>
Date: 2028-06-25T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Late-sprint node tally and deal ops check — HelioFoundry POC

Jonas / team — ran the inventory pass this morning (quick summary below). All numbers are live as of 2028-06-25 08:00 PDT — I'll kick off a more detailed thermal/rack mapping if you want the contiguous placement plan.

US-WEST (primary):
- Total A100-80GB-equivalent free slots: 48
- Largest contiguous block observed: 28 slots (rack-adjacent clusters)
- Short maintenance windows impacting >8 slots: none scheduled in Aug 15–Sep 30

US-CENTRAL (fallback):
- Total free slots: 40
- Largest contiguous block: 32 slots
- Maintenance impacting >8 slots: rolling kernel patching 2028-09-05–09-07 (can be avoided by scheduling start/end dates slightly earlier)

Observations and proposal:
- We don't currently have a single contiguous 32-slot block in us-west; largest is 28.
- Proposed approach: soft-reserve 28 contiguous slots in us-west and 8 slots in us-central. Reserve an extra 4 slots as buffer (total reserved = 40) to protect against last-minute churn and to give Helio headroom for short spikes.
- If Helio insists on a single-region contiguous block, we can offer a commitment to convert a set of us-central racks to us-west-equivalent via network affinity and routing prioritization, but that requires a lead time of ~10 business days and a configuration window.

Attachments: SLA_draft.pdf (internal draft of response to procurement and proposed hold language). I'm happy to convert the numbers into a formal short note for procurement.

Rishi

[attachment: SLA_draft.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Susan Kim <susan.kim@heliofoundry.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: purchasing@heliofoundry.com
Date: 2028-06-26T15:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Late-sprint node tally and deal ops check — HelioFoundry POC

Thanks, team — that data helps. A few quick clarifications from procurement:

- Helio is okay with the split 28/8 approach as long as we have an explicit routing SLA that keeps latency-critical calls to the us-west subset.
- We'd like the 14-day soft-hold documented in writing so our finance team can mark the budget as allocated while legal finishes the SOW. Can you send a short PDF that states the soft-hold mechanics and the conversion timeline to a hard commit?
- If you can commit to bumping the soft-hold to 40 reserved slots (28 us-west + 8 us-central + 4 buffer) for the two-week period, procurement will proceed with internal approvals.

Next steps for Redwood: please send the short hold note and the draft SOW timelines (we've highlighted the MAP_v2.xlsx items that depend on capacity). Once we have those, procurement will confirm and we can schedule the canary deploy.

Susan
HelioFoundry — Cloud Ops
